The retrieved evidence presents two opposing viewpoints: a small set of exceptional case reports claim HIV has been cured in a few individuals via high‑risk stem cell transplants, while mainstream medical and public health authorities state there is no proven cure for HIV and that antiretroviral therapy is lifelong due to viral latency.

On one side, several reports describe rare cures or long‑term remissions in a handful of people following stem cell or bone marrow transplants with specific genetic resistance (CCR5 Δ32), or in exceptional immune control cases, framing HIV cure as feasible in select contexts [d1,d4,d5,d6,d7,d8]. On the other side, authoritative sources explicitly state there is no cure for HIV and that treatment does not eradicate the virus, emphasizing that stopping therapy typically leads to viral rebound because HIV hides in long‑lived latent reservoirs [d10,d11,d12,d13,d14,d15].
